panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real intraoral frontal photograph of the Parry-Romberg syndrome patient described in the disease-focused article. It visibly shows an anterior crossbite on the left side with crowding, i.e. a unilateral occlusal discrepancy consistent with the configured jaw_malocclusion finding (dental malalignment/occlusal deviation). Gingival recession is present but not in the allowed vocabulary, so it is proposed. Attribution rests on the article title and in-text PRS context rather than on facial hemiatrophy, so confidence is moderate. B: Maxillary occlusal photograph of the PRS patient demonstrating unilateral arch asymmetry with constriction of the right side. This one-sided hemimandibular/maxillary asymmetry is the most disease-specific panel and directly matches the configured unilateral jaw malocclusion finding (hemimandibular asymmetry/facial asymmetry with malocclusion), supported by the disease-focused article title and in-text description....

in_text_mentions: Intraoral evaluation revealed mild anterior crowding in both arches, an anterior crossbite on the left side, and gingival recession in the lower anterior region. Both maxillary and mandibular arches showed asymmetry with marked constriction of the right side. The American Board of Orthodontics (ABO) Discrepancy Index [13] confirmed an Class III molar relationship (Figures 2A-2C).
